arxiv-2007-14148.title: Towers and the first-order theory of hyperbolic groups
arxiv-2007-14148.creator: Vincent Guirardel, Gilbert Levitt, Rizos Sklinos
arxiv-2007-14148.description: Abstract This paper is devoted to the first-order theory of torsion-free hyperbolic groups. One of its purposes is to review some results and to provide precise and correct statements and definitions, as well as some proofs and new results. A key concept is that of a tower (Sela) or NTQ system (Kharlampovich-Myasnikov). We discuss them thoroughly.

arxiv-2011-13311.title: Data-Efficient Classification of Radio Galaxies 2021 Data-Efficient Classification of Radio Galaxies – Data Availability
arxiv-2011-13311.creator: Ashwin Samudre, Lijo T. George, Mahak Bansal, Yogesh Wadadekar
arxiv-2011-13311.description: Abstract The continuum emission from radio galaxies can be generally classified into different morphological classes such as FRI, FRII, Bent, or Compact. In this paper, we explore the task of radio galaxy classification based on morphology using deep learning methods with a focus on using a small scale dataset ( ∼ 2000 \sim 2000 samples).

arxiv-2208-04535.title: The structure of 3D collisional magnetized bow shocks in pulsed-power-driven plasma flows
arxiv-2208-04535.creator: R. Datta \aff 1, D. R. Russell \aff 2, I. Tang \aff 2, T. Clayson \aff 2, L. G. Suttle \aff 2, J. P. Chittenden \aff 2, S. V. Lebedev \aff 2, J. D. Hare \aff 1 \corresp
arxiv-2208-04535.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by R. Datta \aff 1, D. R. Russell \aff 2, I. Tang \aff 2, T. Clayson \aff 2, L. G. Suttle \aff 2, J. P. Chittenden \aff 2, S. V. Lebedev \aff 2, J. D. Hare \aff 1 \corresp. We investigate 3D bow shocks in a highly collisional magnetized aluminum plasma, generated during the ablation phase of an exploding wire array on the MAGPIE facility (1.4 MA, 240 ns).

arxiv-2310-00832.title: Natural Language Models for Data Visualization Utilizing nvBench Dataset
arxiv-2310-00832.creator: Shuo Wang and Carlos Crespo-Quinones
arxiv-2310-00832.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Shuo Wang and Carlos Crespo-Quinones. 1
Introduction

Data visualization is an integral part of data analysis and reporting, highly skilled professionals spend a significant portion of their working hours constructing data queries and turning them into charts and graphs. The potential application of machine learning models to understand the underlying data and translate natural language queries into data visualization would greatly enhance the efficiency and productivity of many data analysis tasks.

arxiv-2501-01310.title: Systematic Search for Long-Term Trends in Fermi -LAT Jetted Active Galactic Nuclei astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , fermipy software package ( Wood et al. 2017 ) , statsmodels ( Seabold & Perktold 2010 ) https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/index.html
arxiv-2501-01310.creator: P. Peñil, A. Domínguez, S. Buson, M. Ajello, S. Adhikari, A. Rico
arxiv-2501-01310.description: Abstract Jetted Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) exhibit variability across a wide range of time scales. Traditionally, this variability can often be modeled well as a stochastic process. However, in certain cases, jetted AGN variability displays regular patterns, enabling us to conduct investigations aimed at understanding its origins.

arxiv-2505-11711.title: Reinforcement Learning Finetunes Small Subnetworks in Large Language Models
arxiv-2505-11711.creator: Sagnik Mukherjee, Lifan Yuan, Dilek Hakkani-Tür, Hao Peng, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, {sagnikm3, lifan4, dilek, haopeng}@illinois.edu
arxiv-2505-11711.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning (RL) yields substantial improvements in large language models’ (LLMs) downstream task performance and alignment with human values. Surprisingly, such large gains result from updating only a small subnetwork comprising just 5%-30% of the parameters, with the rest effectively unchanged. We refer to this phenomenon as parameter update sparsity induced by RL.

arxiv-2509-10406.title: Multipole Semantic Attention: A Fast Approximation of Softmax Attention for Pretraining
arxiv-2509-10406.creator: Rupert Mitchell, Kristian Kersting
arxiv-2509-10406.description: Abstract We present Multipole Semantic Attention (MuSe), an efficient approximation of softmax attention that combines semantic clustering with multipole expansions from computational physics. Our method addresses the quadratic computational complexity of transformers in the context length by clustering queries and keys separately in their learned representation spaces, enabling a hierarchical two-stage attention mechanism.

arxiv-2509-13317.title: 3D Aware Region Prompted Vision Language Model
arxiv-2509-13317.creator: An-Chieh Cheng, Yang Fu, Yukang Chen, Zhijian Liu, Xiaolong Li, Subhashree Radhakrishnan, Song Han, Yao Lu, Jan Kautz, Pavlo Molchanov, Hongxu Yin, Xiaolong Wang, Sifei Liu
arxiv-2509-13317.description: Abstract We present S patial R egion 3D ( SR-3D ) aware vision–language model that connects single-view 2D images and multi-view 3D data through a shared visual token space. SR-3D supports flexible region prompting, allowing users to annotate regions with bounding boxes, segmentation masks on any frame, or directly in 3D, without the need for exhaustive multi-frame labeling.

arxiv-2601-02419.title: How Alice, long before her time, derived the principles of quantum mechanics.
arxiv-2601-02419.creator: Marcello Poletti
arxiv-2601-02419.description: Abstract This philosophical dialogue explores the idea that the foundational principles of quantum mechanics need not be interpreted as describing a new physics, but may instead arise from the logical necessity of formalising the act of measurement within a coherent algebraic framework.

arxiv-2601-14791.title: Synthetic Data Augmentation for Multi-Task Chinese Porcelain Classification: A Stable Diffusion Approach
arxiv-2601-14791.creator: Ziyao Ling, Silvia Mirri, Paola Salomoni, Giovanni Delnevo
arxiv-2601-14791.description: Abstract The scarcity of training data presents a fundamental challenge in applying deep learning to archaeological artifact classification, particularly for the rare types of Chinese porcelain. This study investigates whether synthetic images generated through Stable Diffusion with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) can effectively augment limited real datasets for multi-task CNN-based porcelain classification.

arxiv-2602-15517.title: A Model Order Reduction Method for Seismic Applications Using the Laplace Transform
arxiv-2602-15517.creator: Fernando Henríquez, Matthias Schlottbom
arxiv-2602-15517.description: Abstract We devise and analyze a reduced basis model order reduction (MOR) strategy for an abstract wave problem with vanishing initial conditions and a source term given by the product of a temporal Ricker wavelet and a spatial profile. Such wave problems comprise the acoustic and elastic wave equations, with applications in seismic modeling.

pmc-11507985.title: Composition of Higher Alcohols in Different Alcoholic Beverages and Their Metabolic Dynamics in Bama Pigs
pmc-11507985.creator: Xiaonian Cao, Yunfei Hou, Qingqing Liu, Qian Yang, Min Liu, Haixu Lin, Qingxi Ren, Jian Mao, Raquel Rodríguez Solana
pmc-11507985.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The unique flavour contribution of higher alcohols in alcoholic beverages has received growing attention; however, there is a dearth of information on their in vivo metabolic kinetics. In this study, the composition and content of higher alcohols in different alcoholic beverages from Chinese Baijiu and Lujiu were studied via in vivo analysis using Bama pigs to elucidate the mechanisms for intoxication of alcohol in vitro and in drinkers.

pmc-11675783.title: Development of Eco-Friendly Packaging Films from Soyhull Lignocellulose: Towards Valorizing Agro-Industrial Byproducts
pmc-11675783.creator: Sumi Regmi, Sandeep Paudel, Srinivas Janaswamy
pmc-11675783.description: Due to their inability to biodegrade, petroleum-based plastics pose significant environmental challenges by disrupting aquatic, marine, and terrestrial ecosystems. Additionally, the widespread presence of microplastics and nanoplastics induces serious health risks for humans and animals. These pressing issues create an urgent need for designing and developing eco-friendly, biodegradable, renewable, and non-toxic plastic alternatives.

pmc-12651197.title: Multifaceted Effects of Thymoquinone on Platelet Calcium Homeostasis
pmc-12651197.creator: Natalia Rukoyatkina, Igor Mindukshev, Diana M Mikhailova, Mikhail A Panteleev, Stepan Gambaryan, Smaragdi Antonopoulou
pmc-12651197.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Highlights What are the main findings? Thymoquinone (TQ) strongly and acutely inhibited agonist-induced platelet activation and aggregation. TQ differentially regulates GPCR and GPVI receptor activation by enhancing [Ca2+]i mobilization by GPCR-induced activation and inhibition of GPVI-induced [Ca2+]i mobi-lization.Presented data are the first example in which complete inhibition of ADP- and Trap-6-, but not CRP-induced, aggregation is accompanied by high [Ca2+]i levels. What is the implication of the main finding?

pmc-13049410.title: A plastic surgery approach to Meige syndrome: Botulinum toxin for rebalancing facial dystonia and aesthetics – A case report
pmc-13049410.creator: Xiao Long
pmc-13049410.description: Meige syndrome is a rare segmental dystonia characterized by blepharospasm and oromandibular dystonia, often leading to significant functional and aesthetic impairment. This report details a 59-year-old female patient with a 16-year history whose symptoms were refractory to prior drug therapies.

pmc-13194345.title: Editorial: The role of innate immunity in the pathogenesis of autoimmune and autoinflammatory diseases
pmc-13194345.creator: Carmelo Carmona-Rivera, Diana Gómez-Martín, José Luis Maravillas-Montero, José Jiram Torres-Ruiz
pmc-13194345.description: esearch Topic collectively support a conceptual shift that positions innate immunity as a key player of disease initiation, amplification, and tissue injury. Despite employing diverse methodologies, including mechanistic studies, omics analyses, clinical investigations, and systematic reviews, all articles converge on the view that innate immune dysregulation is fundamental across autoimmune and autoinflammatory diseases.

pmc-13394736.title: Multidisciplinary Treatment for Esophagogastric Junction Cancer From a Dutch Perspective
pmc-13394736.creator: Hidde C. G. Overtoom, Suzanne S. Gisbertz
pmc-13394736.description: Esophagogastric junction (EGJ) cancer is an increasing health burden worldwide. Over the past decade, significant advancements in centralization, multimodal treatment strategies, as well as the widespread adoption of minimally invasive surgical techniques, have led to marked improvements in perioperative outcomes and overall survival of EGJ cancer in the Netherlands.

pmc-13628224.title: Engineered naringenin-loaded nanoscale coordination polymers for targeted treatment of acute kidney injury
pmc-13628224.creator: Li-Bin Zhou, Min-Zhi Zhou, Yan-Guo Li, Zong-Jian Wu, Xuan-Ze Peng, Yang Sun, Hai-Bo Mao, Hui-Min Long, Min Yin, Xue-Ying Tan, Jian-Ting Xu, Jing-Bo Hu
pmc-13628224.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a severe clinical condition lacking targeted and effective pharmacotherapies. Dysregulated inflammation, largely driven by the nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling pathway, is a primary mediator of tubular damage in AKI. While bioinformatic and preliminary analyses identified the natural flavonoid naringenin (Nag) as a potent NF-κB inhibitor, its therapeutic utility is severely restricted by poor aqueous solubility, rapid systemic metabolism, and insufficient renal accumulation.

pmc-13633387.title: Cell Blocks and the Milan System for Reporting Salivary Gland Cytopathology: A Meta‐Analysis
pmc-13633387.creator: Aada Närhi, David Kalfert, Henri Lagerstam, Ivana Kholová
pmc-13633387.description: BackgroundThe Milan System for Reporting Salivary Gland Cytopathology (MSRSGC) is a classification system first released in 2018. It provides a standardized categorization for salivary gland lesions. Cell blocks can be prepared from fine‐needle aspirations (FNAs) and can be utilized for the diagnostics of salivary gland lesions.
